questions.text: Let A(1:8, -5:5, -10:5) be a three dimensional array. How many elements are there in the array A?
questions.solution: Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

Each element is enqueued once and can be dequeued at most once. Across n operations, the total dequeues (including those inside MultiDequeue) cannot exceed the number of enqueues.

Total work = [latex]\Theta(n)[/latex] (amortised).

Answer: [latex]\Theta(n)[/latex]
